# Psalm 57 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 57:3 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** I-call to-God Most-High, to-the-God who-accomplishes [all things] for-me.
- **LOGOS:** I cry out to God Most High, to God who fulfills His purpose for me.
- **PNEUMA:** I cry out to God Most High, to God who will fulfill His purpose for me.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 57:7 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** A-net they-prepared for-my-steps — my-soul bowed-down; they-dug before-me a-pit — they-fell into-its-midst. Selah.
- **LOGOS:** They set a net for my steps; my soul was bowed down. They dug a pit in my way, but they have fallen into it themselves. Selah.
- **PNEUMA:** My enemies have set a trap for me. I am weary from distress. They have dug a deep pit in my path, but they themselves have fallen into it! Pause and reflect.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 57:8 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** My-heart is-steadfast, O-God, my-heart is-steadfast; I-will-sing and-make-music.
- **LOGOS:** My heart is steadfast, O God, my heart is steadfast! I will sing and make melody!
- **PNEUMA:** My heart is confident in You, O God; my heart is confident. No wonder I can sing Your praises!

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

- **EMET:** For-the-choirmaster. Al-Tashcheth [Do-Not-Destroy]. Of-David. A-Miktam, when-he-fled from-before Saul in-the-cave.
- **LOGOS:** For the choirmaster. According to Do Not Destroy. A Miktam of David, when he fled from Saul, in the cave.
- **PNEUMA:** For the music director. A psalm of David, regarding the time he fled from Saul and went into the cave. To the tune of 'Do Not Destroy.'

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 57:4 (overlap: 4%)

- **EMET:** He-sends from-heaven and-saves-me; He-puts-to-shame the-one-who-tramples-me. Selah. God sends His-steadfast-love and-His-truth.
- **LOGOS:** He will send from heaven and save me; He will put to shame him who tramples on me. Selah. God will send out His steadfast love and His faithfulness!
- **PNEUMA:** He will send help from heaven to rescue me, disgracing those who hound me. Pause and reflect. My God will send forth His unfailing love and faithfulness.
